patch.value: GH-1135: item_hash_version 2 still masks writer hash divergence as corruption

GitHub #1135 reproduces supported pm writers computing different history hashes while stamping the same item_hash_version=2, so pinned readers classify version skew as hash/chain corruption and history-repair can truthfully report changed=false while rewriting bytes.

A released-version fixture proves whether identical epoch-2 content can hash differently; every hash-input or algorithm change advances a format capability or preserves the previous comparator; drift diagnostics distinguish unsupported writer/version skew from same-version corruption; history events expose sufficient writer capability provenance for deterministic diagnosis; repair changed receipts match actual byte writes; SDK CLI health validate and repair contracts carry the distinction; focused cross-version packed-consumer and exact repository coverage gates pass
Global pm 2026.8.23 writes trackers read by repository-pinned 2026.8.20 and 2026.8.21 binaries

Create and mutate an item with pm 2026.8.23, run pinned health --strict-exit, compare item_hash_version and hashes, run pinned history-repair, then compare changed receipt, bytes, and both readers' verdicts.
Supported readers attribute incompatible persisted hash capabilities as version skew, and repair never reports a no-op when bytes changed.
Three repositories reproduced opposite integrity verdicts while both writers stamped item_hash_version 2; pinned repair rewrote the stream despite changed=false and inverted which reader accepted it.
